title_en: The mirage and the layered darkness
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The mirage and the darkness over the deep sea

claims.statement_en: The ayah says that those who disbelieve have deeds like a mirage in a plain: the thirsty one thinks it is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, who pays him his account in full; and God is swift in reckoning.

The ayah then gives a further picture, introduced by the word or: the deeds are like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which is a cloud: darknesses, some above others; when one reaches out he can hardly see what he reaches with.
The ayah ends by saying that whoever God gives no light has no light.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah likens the deeds of those who disbelieve to a mirage in a plain, which the thirsty one takes for water but finds to be nothing [c1]. It then gives a picture of darknesses over a deep sea, and says that whoever God gives no light has no light [c2][c3].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah says that those who disbelieve have deeds like a mirage in a plain [c1]. The thirsty one thinks it is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing [c1]. He finds God with him, who pays him his account in full, and God is swift in reckoning [c1].

The ayah then gives a further picture, introduced by the word or: the deeds are like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is another wave, above which is a cloud: darknesses, some above others [c2]. When one holds out what is before him he can hardly see it [c2]. The ayah ends by saying that whoever God gives no light has no light [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah gives pictures joined by the word or, and the ayat do not say whether they are alternatives or further descriptions of the same deeds [c1][c2]. In the first the thirsty one finds nothing where he looked for water, and finds God with him [c1]. In the picture of the sea the darkness is layered, and the ayah closes with the statement about light [c2][c3].
chapters.kids_md: The ayah says that the deeds of those who disbelieve are like a mirage in a plain [c1]. The thirsty one thinks it is water, but when he comes to it he finds it to be nothing [c1]. The ayah also gives a picture of darknesses over a deep sea, with a wave above a wave and a cloud above them [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the mirage shows something that looks like water from far off and is found to be nothing on arrival [c1]. Another reading is that the ayah ends by saying that whoever God gives no light has no light [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which deeds are meant or who in particular is meant; no person is named.
- Not established: where the plain or the deep sea is, or what the layers of darkness stand for beyond the picture.
- The ayat do not use the word mathal here: they give similes with the word like. That this item is grouped with the parables is the platform's classification, not the text's.
- The sense of the word or in 24:40 is read as an alternative or as an addition; this draft leaves it open.
- The Arabic of 24:40 names a part of the body that reaches out; this draft says 'reaches out' and keeps that part general.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: none identified; a scholar should say whether any should be linked to these ayat.
The sense of the word or in 24:40 and the wording of the reaching-out part in 24:40 are for a scholar to decide.
